instructions: Off the heat, whisk the 2 cups oat flour, the 2 cups milk and 2 1/2 cups water together in a large pot until no lumps are left.
Add a pinch of salt and the 2 cinnamon sticks.
Set the pot over medium-low heat. Stir often and scrape the bottom so it doesn't stick or burn. Cook for 15 to 20 minutes, until it thickens to a loose, velvety porridge.
Take the pot off the heat, lift out the cinnamon sticks and stir in the honey.
Serve hot in bowls or mugs.
method_notes: The Bale Moya version leads: oat flour, milk, water, cinnamon and honey, stirred over medium-low heat for 15 to 20 minutes. Ethiopian-Food.org's Gebs Atmit uses roasted barley flour and water with a little honey (5 stars from 2 reviews), and ChildFund's uses oat powder with milk and sugar; all of them whisk the flour in smooth and stir often. None has 20 ratings, so this counts as a fallback. Atmit is often drunk rather than eaten with a spoon, so thin it with a splash of milk if you like. Barley flour or niter kibbeh are not used here.
